purpose: Teach: 念仏/党派/連隊/中退/白血病/リンパ/邁進/衰弱

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、念仏宗の歴史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Sakura, you wrote your paper on the history of Pure Land Buddhism, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, acknowledging tone. Slight upward inflection—not quite a question, more like confirmation. Steady eye contact. Patient. The cadence of a teacher who remembers each student's work.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、戦前の党派対立を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I focused on factional conflict in the prewar period.
lines.style: Clear and direct. Sits up slightly. Respectful but not deferential. A student offering their work without apology. Even pacing, slight emphasis on 'prewar.'

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 近代軍の連隊編制を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And the regimental structure of the modern military—that was in your paper as well?
lines.style: Thoughtful pause before speaking. Softer inflection. The tone of someone genuinely curious about the connections the student found. Unhurried.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、高校中退者の社会復帰を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I examined social reintegration for high school dropouts.
lines.style: Steady voice. Meets the question without hesitation. Matter-of-fact but not detached. Shows she knows her own work and where it leads.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 白血病治療の歴史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: The history of leukemia treatment—that was part of your scope too?
lines.style: Engaged, genuine interest. Leans forward slightly. The phrasing shows recognition of breadth. Warm without being leading. Inviting the student to expand.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、リンパ系免疫の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I looked at lymphatic immune system research.
lines.style: Quiet confidence. No overexplanation. The answer of someone who has thought through her material. Slight lift at the end, open rather than closed.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 教育者が邁進した道のりを論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And the path educators took in their pursuit of that work?
lines.style: Reflective, slower pace. Gentler inflection. The question draws inward—almost musing aloud. Respect for the depth of the investigation. Not pressing, just wondering.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、長期療養者の衰弱を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I investigated the physical decline in patients undergoing long-term recovery.
lines.style: Final answer with clarity and completeness. Grounded tone. Breath at the end but not trailing off—it's a full stop. The sense of a student finishing her thought with quiet authority.
